# Fit a straight line (stats.regress)

## categories

[
  "statistics",
  "math"
]

## demonstrations

[
  {
    "expected_output": {
      "count": 3,
      "intercept": 1,
      "r": 1,
      "slope": 2
    },
    "id": "straight-line",
    "input": {
      "x": [
        0,
        1,
        2
      ],
      "y": [
        1,
        3,
        5
      ]
    },
    "title": "An exact straight-line relationship"
  },
  {
    "expected_output": {
      "count": 3,
      "intercept": 7,
      "r": null,
      "slope": 0
    },
    "id": "constant-y",
    "input": {
      "x": [
        1,
        2,
        3
      ],
      "y": [
        7,
        7,
        7
      ]
    },
    "title": "Constant response has undefined correlation"
  }
]

## description

Fit a line with an intercept to paired finite numeric lists x and y of equal length. Return count, slope, intercept and Pearson correlation r. Constant x is rejected because the line is not identifiable. For constant y and nonconstant x, return slope 0, intercept equal to that constant and r null (undefined correlation). Duplicate x values are allowed if x is not entirely constant. The computation normalizes numeric scales before using standard-library regression and correlation, then transforms the line back. Outputs are rounded floating-point values. No code, files or expressions are accepted.

## failure_modes

  },
  {
    "condition": "The fitted result exceeds finite floating-point range.",
    "recovery": "Rescale the numeric observations and state the units used.",
    "symptom": "Capability error; no infinite result is returned."
  }
]

## limitations

[
  "2 to 10000 finite numbers per list, equal lengths, each number between -1e12 and 1e12 inclusive. Booleans, numeric strings and expressions are rejected.",
  "Constant x is not identifiable and is rejected; constant y has r null. No missing-value filtering is performed.",
  "Outputs use binary floating point; results outside finite floating-point range are rejected, and rounding or underflow may affect extreme scales.",
  "This is a descriptive OLS fit with an intercept, not a causal finding, uncertainty estimate or significance test."
]

Fit a straight line

## summary

Fit y = slope*x + intercept by ordinary least squares and report Pearson r.
